A "now hiring" sign in the window, a stack of resumes by the register, three job board logins with three different inboxes. Knowing how to post a job is the easy part. Writing a post that earns applications, putting it in front of the right people, and keeping track of everyone who responds is what eats your week.


This guide covers each step: writing the post, choosing where to post it, publishing to several job boards at once, letting walk-ins apply with a QR code, and managing applicants once they arrive.

A job post that fills the role comes down to a clear post, the right boards, and a fast reply.


- **Write for candidates.** Use the title people search for, include pay, and state the schedule.

## **How to Post a Job (Step by Step)**


The best way to post a job is to define the role, write a clear post with pay and schedule, publish it on the boards your candidates use, and review applicants every day. Here are the five steps.


### **Step 1: Define the Role and Requirements**


List the three to five duties this person will handle each day. Separate must-haves from nice-to-haves, because disguising preferences as requirements scares off qualified candidates.


Settle the schedule and the pay before you write anything. Salary data from Glassdoor or Payscale shows what similar roles pay in your area.


### **Step 2: Write a Clear, Concise Job Posting**


Use a title candidates actually type into a search bar, like "Marketing Coordinator" instead of "Marketing Ninja." Add a short summary, list duties in order of importance, and include the schedule and pay. The next section breaks down what each part should say.


### **Step 3: Choose Where to Post Your Job**


Indeed and ZipRecruiter reach the widest hourly audience. LinkedIn suits professional roles, and Facebook reaches local candidates. Add the job to your own website too, since candidates who arrive directly tend to be more engaged. If you are not sure where to start, see our list of[top job boards for hourly workers](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/top-job-boards-hourly-workers) .


Posting to each board by hand takes a separate account and form every time.[Post to five job boards in one click](https://www.joinhomebase.com/hiring-and-onboarding) with Homebase, free on every plan.


### **Step 4: Publish and Promote the Job**


Share the post in local Facebook groups, on Nextdoor and with your team. A small referral bonus gets employees sharing. Pay for promotion only when the role is hard to fill or urgent, and start with a small budget to test results.


### **Step 5: Review Applicants and Follow Up**


Review applications daily and sort them into strong, maybe and not a fit. Reply to strong candidates within 24 to 48 hours. The best people interview in several places and accept the first solid offer.


## **What to Say in a Job Posting**


A strong job posting includes a searchable title, a short role summary, duties in order of importance, must-have qualifications, schedule details, a pay range and clear application steps. For ideas, browse these[job posting examples](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/job-posting-examples) .


### **Job Title and Role Summary**


Match the title to what candidates search for, not your internal terminology. If a qualifier matters, like weekends only, put it in the title.


Then write two to three sentences covering the job, the daily work and why it is a good one: "We're hiring a full-time barista for our busy downtown coffee shop. You'll make espresso drinks, take orders and welcome our regulars."


### **Responsibilities and Qualifications**


List five to eight duties, each starting with an action verb. Then split qualifications into must-haves, like a valid driver's license, and nice-to-haves, labeled "preferred." Our Lead Talent Acquisition Advisor, Josh Dunton, keeps it simple: "I would never prioritize nice-to-haves." See a full example in this[line cook job description](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/line-cook-job-description) .


### **Schedule Expectations**


Say whether the job is full-time, part-time or variable, which days and shifts it covers, and how much flexibility you offer. State whether the role is for a[regular employee](https://www.joinhomebase.com/glossary/regular-employee) or a[temporary](https://www.joinhomebase.com/glossary/temporary-employee) or seasonal worker.


### **Pay Range**


Include pay even when your state does not require it. Employers in New York with four or more employees must[list compensation ranges](https://www.dol.ny.gov/pay-transparency) , and other states have similar rules. Ranges also draw more applicants. If you cannot give an exact range, a starting point like "Starting at $18 an hour, with raises based on performance" sets expectations. Use the same range on every board.


### **How to Apply**


Keep the application simple and say what happens next, such as "We review applications on a rolling basis and reach out within 3 to 5 business days."


## **Where to Post a Job Online**


Different boards work for different roles, budgets and timelines. Here is how to post on the most common ones. For a longer comparison, see the[best job posting sites for employers](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/best-job-posting-sites-for-employers) .


### **How to Post a Job on Indeed**


Indeed is the largest job board, so it is a solid starting point for most roles. To post, create an employer account, click **Post a Job** , enter the job details and description, choose free or sponsored, and publish.[Indeed's employer guide](https://www.indeed.com/hire/resources/howtohub/how-to-post-a-job-on-indeed) walks through each screen.


You can post up to 3 hosted jobs a month for free. Indeed reviews each post, which usually takes 24 to 48 hours, and free posts are most visible in the first two to three days. Sponsored jobs stay more visible. You set the budget and pay when someone engages with your job. Indeed does not accept duplicate listings from multiple sources, so post each job once.


### **How to Post a Job on LinkedIn**


LinkedIn works best for professional roles where candidates are building a career. It is less effective for shift workers, who tend to search elsewhere.


You can have one free job active at a time. A free post stays live for up to 14 days, and LinkedIn typically caps free posts at 10 to 30 applications depending on the role.[LinkedIn's help center](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a517777) lists the current limits. Promote a post when you are competing for specialized talent.


### **How to Post a Job on Facebook**


Facebook works well for local, hourly roles like servers, retail associates and child care providers. You can create a[Facebook job listing](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/10/introducing-local-jobs-facebook/) through Marketplace, your Page or Meta Business Suite. You can also share the post in local job groups. Photos and video show off your workplace.


### **Google for Jobs**


Google for Jobs is not a place to post. It is a search feature that pulls listings from job boards and career pages. Boards like Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter and Glassdoor feed it automatically. Your own careers page can qualify with[job posting structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/job-posting) , but that takes a developer.


### **Upwork for Freelance Work**


Upwork connects you with freelancers and contractors for project work, like design, copywriting or virtual assistant tasks. It is not built for employees who work on site.

Here is how it works:


1. Write one complete post with the title, pay range, schedule and must-haves.
2. Choose the boards. For hourly roles, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, Facebook and Craigslist are the usual picks, and Google picks up listings on its own.
3. Publish from one place. In Homebase, open the Hiring page, describe the role and post it.
4. Allow time for review. Posts usually go live within 2 hours to 3 days, depending on each board's review. Each one stays active for 30 days, and you get a reminder before it expires.
5. Review every applicant in one list instead of four inboxes.
6. Spot-check each listing once it is live. Confirm the pay range matches everywhere and that no duplicate has appeared.


Primo Stropoli, owner of Tetta's Market, describes it this way: "In a couple clicks I could just have a post out there and start receiving applicants. It's really hard to measure just how valuable that is."


Posting everywhere also means more places to keep accurate. Keep the pay range identical on every board, and edit the job in one spot so changes carry through. Homebase notes that updates can take 1 to 3 business days to show on the boards.

## **How to Let Walk-Ins Apply With a QR Code**


Put a QR code for your job post where walk-ins already look: the door, the counter, the takeout bag. They scan it, apply on their phones and land in the same applicant list as everyone else. You never retype a paper application. It also gives you an answer when someone asks, "Are you hiring?" during a rush, which can turn into a[walk-in interview](https://www.joinhomebase.com/glossary/walk-in-interview) on the spot.


Here is how to set it up in Homebase:


1. Post the job first. Your business needs a valid physical address and a website or official Facebook Page, and new accounts are reviewed before posts go out, so your first post can take a little longer.
2. From the Hiring page, open the **Manage** menu on the job card to copy the job link, or download the job's QR code.
3. For walk-ins who would rather text, add your Text-to-Apply code. You can find it on your Career Page, and it sends a link to your application by text.
4. Print the code with a short call to action, such as "Scan to apply."
5. Place it at the door, the register, the break room, on flyers and on business cards.
6. Review these applicants alongside your job board applicants in the Hiring dashboard. The Source filter shows which ones came from the QR code.


Andrew Davis, a franchise owner at Scooter's Coffee, hired about 90% of his team through the Homebase job posting link, including referrals. Referrals went through that same link, so every applicant landed in one list.


If walk-ins are a big part of how you hire,[post a job free with Homebase](https://app.joinhomebase.com/onboarding/sign-up) and print your code today.

## **Common Job Posting Mistakes to Avoid**


- **Vague job titles:** "Team Member" or "Associate" does not tell candidates what the job involves.
- **Missing pay info:** Leaving out pay costs you applications, and some states require it.
- **Overloaded requirements:** A long list with no "preferred" labels scares off qualified people. Mention training if you offer it.
- **Unclear schedules:** "Full-time, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with occasional evening events" gives candidates what they need to decide.
- **Mismatched pay ranges:** The same job showing different pay on different boards erodes trust.
- **No follow-up process:** If you take weeks to respond, strong candidates accept offers elsewhere.


## **How to Manage Applicants After You Post Your Job**


Having a plan keeps a full inbox from feeling like a second job:


1. Block time each day to review applicants.
2. Sort them into strong yes, maybe and no, and move strong candidates to screening right away.
3. Send an acknowledgment when each application arrives, such as "Thanks for applying, we'll reach out by Friday."
4. Offer several interview times or use self-service scheduling.
5. Confirm interviews 24 hours ahead and tell candidates if you need more time to decide.


Josh Dunton, Lead Talent Acquisition Advisor at Homebase, sums up a good candidate experience in three things: "Authentic interactions, efficient and timely processes and actionable feedback." Adding[screening questions](https://www.joinhomebase.com/hiring-and-onboarding/applicant-screening) to your post helps you reach the people worth interviewing first.


## **Frequently Asked Questions About Posting a Job**


### **How Can I Post One Job Listing to Multiple Job Boards at Once?**


Write the job once and publish it through a hiring tool that sends it to several boards at the same time. Homebase posts to Indeed, ZipRecruiter, Google, Facebook and Craigslist in one click and collects applicants in one list. Posting by hand means repeating the form and checking each board separately.


### **What Is the Best Way to Post a Job?**


Write a clear post with pay and schedule, then publish it where your candidates already search. For hourly roles that usually means Indeed, ZipRecruiter and Facebook. Posting to several boards at once reaches more people with less work, and replying to applicants within 48 hours keeps strong candidates from taking other offers.


### **How Do I Post a Job for Free?**


Indeed lets you post up to three hosted jobs a month for free. LinkedIn allows one active free job at a time. Facebook posting costs nothing, and Homebase posts to five boards at no charge on every plan. Free listings lose visibility over time, so check that they are still getting views.


### **What Should a Job Posting Include?**


Include a searchable job title, a short role summary, duties in order of importance, must-have qualifications, schedule details, a pay range and clear application steps. Label nice-to-haves separately so candidates can judge their fit. Several states require a pay range, so include one even where the law does not.


### **How Much Does It Cost to Post a Job on Indeed?**


Posting on Indeed is free for up to three hosted jobs a month. Sponsored jobs are optional: you set the budget and pay when someone engages with your job. Free posts are most visible in the first two to three days, so sponsor hard-to-fill roles.


### **How Do Walk-In Applicants Apply With a QR Code?**


Print the QR code for your job post and place it at the door or counter. Applicants scan it with a phone, fill out the application, and appear in your applicant list next to candidates from job boards. You never retype a paper form.
